Creating recipes is annoying at times, and if you accidentally add an ingredient during recipe creation, there is no way to remove it. I usually just change the amount to 1gram so it doesn’t really impact the overall calories too much. But it’s annoying.

The AI feature gets it wrong 60% of the time. I get it’s not a perfect feature, but I have seen this be more intuitive in other apps.

Would really consider other apps, and I will not be using this one once my subscription ends.

reviews.title: Don’t get a membership
reviews.text:
I paid for a year membership.
I should be able to delete a weight log for any day. I should not have to enter a new weight log for the day that I’m trying to delete when it’s a mistake.
For an example (that actually happened today) if I didn’t weigh myself on August 5, and I accidentally log a weight for that day I should be able to delete it. Because now my progress is going to be messed up because I can’t fix it.
I should be able to customize if I want to see whatever a “true weight” is especially when I weight myself at the same time, if not everyday, every other day. I know my true weight. I don’t want to see what the app “thinks” my weight is.
I should also be able to have the option of a trial period AT THE LEAST because I absolutely hate this app. I want a refund, honestly, because keeping a journal is easier than maneuvering this app, giving me a body complex, and an eating disorder wasn’t on my list of things to accomplish by trying to utilize this app. 
Using the tools to log the food you have eaten is a nightmare, especially if you eat the same food(s) throughout the week. If you don’t “create a recipe” or “save” it, there is a lot of back and forth between days that is created. I’m probably not describing it well, but it’s completely unnecessary. It’s literally easier to flip back and forth in a written journal than it is to use this stupidly, expensive app.
If I could give negative stars I would.

reviews.title: So innacurate and hard to use
reviews.text: Genuinely how does this app have good reviews? I paid for a yearly subscription because it was cheaper. I assumed all these apps that have a good rating would probably be good at counting calories and macros. This is horrible. It doesn’t have a good database. I can’t even put in a chipotle bowl and it knows what it is. And then it will be so inaccurate. It told me the white rice from chipotle is 13 g of protein. That’s obviously wrong. Then the double adobo chicken it listed at like 39 g of protein when chipotle literally lists it at 64 g. Taking a picture does not help. It’s completely wrong on even how much the serving size is. And then the apps UX is horrible. I should just be able to re-enter the macros if I literally know it, but they make that impossible. I literally have to make a whole custom food. I can’t just start from a base and then change the details I got wrong. If there is a way to do that, they made it impossible to know. Waste of $20 gonna go get another app.

reviews.title: Do not recommend for long term use
reviews.text:
This app worked great for the first 3–4 months, but then it suddenly stopped working without any warning. I reached out to the support team multiple times, but aside from receiving a couple of what appeared to be automated AI responses that simply repeated the same message, I haven’t received any meaningful assistance. Those responses eventually stopped as well, and it’s now been two days with no communication.

Because of the lack of support, I’ll be canceling my subscription and switching to MyFitnessPal. I wanted to avoid the mainstream option and support a newer company, but unfortunately that hasn’t worked out. In hindsight, I probably should have gone with the more established platform from the beginning.

To make matters worse, I paid for a full year of service and only got about 3–4 months of reliable use. At this point, I’ve accepted that I’m probably out the money. I just want an app that’s dependable and backed by responsive customer support.

reviews.text:
I downloaded this app to compare it to the Lose it app I use.  
I thought with it being an Apple based app I would love it.  
I went through all the prompts answering all the questions honestly and paid twenty dollars for a month use, thankfully I had enough sense not to pay for a year.  
It pulled up my plan and I was shocked at the amount of calories it told me I should eat.  I would definitely gain weight at that rate. But the worst part is I started to try to add what I ate so far that day.  It claims that their AI is extremely accurate. Haha! Not!  I literally took a picture of the nutrition label on my protein shake and it logged totally incorrect information.   I tried again and it did it again.  I tried typing in protein shake but it kept coming up with the wrong information.  I was frustrated and just gave up, cancelled my subscription and deleted the app.  
If you want a great calorie tracker, use Lose it!!

Other Calorie Counters have a much wider range of food options. For example, I was trying to find a specific protein powder that wasn’t available in this Calorie Counter. I couldn’t figure out how to add custom calories either. Scanning the labels didn’t work, even though calories were clearly listed on the labels. It would still default list the foods at 0 cal.

On the bright side, at least let me input custom amounts of ounces And other measurements. The UI design was pretty clean too.

Absolutely the worst calorie tracking app I’ve ever used. Wish I hadn’t wasted my time and money.

reviews.title: Not Very Encapsulating
reviews.text: Honestly outside of the AI for tracking this app is like the worst for encouraging weight loss.  The questions for creating guidelines to your needs and expectations don’t incorporate systematic issues or mental health issues that attribute to weight gain.  For instance the options for how many times you eat in a day was 1,2,3,4+.  As a person with adhd some days it’s a day full of snacks, other days I might totally forget to eat.  Also the BMI scale is super inaccurate for tall and short people.  It also isn’t a diversely effective way of measuring populations as it’s solely based off research of white men.  I’ll stick with MyFitnessPal.

reviews.text:
I never bother to write reviews but given the price I thought it was important. Very few foods have been correctly uploaded to the app particularly in the UK.  When adding new foods the app continually does not save the details, meaning I have to add them again over and over again. reviews.title: Don’t waste your money
reviews.text: One of the worse, most over complicated, frustrating and manual labour calorie counting apps I’ve ever used. The AI does not recognise the food, meal or source. When you scan or load a food source or brand into the app it registers the wrong macros. Not worth the time or effort. There’s plenty of other tools on the market that does a much better job without charging a cent.

reviews.title: Frustrating
reviews.text:
My grievance with this app comes down to two points. The first is the logging UI. In an attempt to be sleek and stylish, it end up being confusing and frustrating. Once there is any sort of history, it becomes difficult to tell what is an option to log and what’s already been looked. I spent more time double-checking the system than actually logging. 

My second issue is the prescription. I feel like this was designed specifically on the initial log in to obscure there were other options/plans. It went straight to yearly.
It wasn’t until I was in the app and playing with options that I discovered the other plans. It deceptive and predatory. 

They should have been a trial. Maybe a week. That way I could have found issue one before they stole a year subscription from me. 

I don’t recommend this app. There are better out there.

reviews.title: Says free but it’s not
reviews.text: Went all through registration then it wanted to charge me. Total con.

reviews.title: Massively over complicated
reviews.text:
You have to pile in a huge amount it data, subscribe to the service, and you’re prompted to rate the app before you’ve even used it.
I drink tea with milk each day. This adds to my calorie count. Can I add it? Nah. Not at all. It lacks basic functionality…. Oh, but it has AI in it…. 
No. This is a waste of time and effort. Don’t been duped into a long signup. They will take your cash before you know what the app does.
This practice is disgusting and I cannot accept it as being ok.
You don’t go into a shop, hand them a chunk of cash then be given a mystery item, so why is it ok here?

reviews.title: Shockingly bad
reviews.text: I bought this app assuming it would track fiber, which is a key micronutrient. It does not. That was pretty shocking to me as fiber is pretty basic and is included in literally all other food trackers I’ve ever used. But then when I asked the app support to make sure I wasn’t just missing it, the app support person lied and told me that the app did track fiber, and gave me specific instructions for how to find it. Only after I told them that those instructions didn’t work did they walk it back and say actually the app does not track fiber after all. Really unbelievably insane for the specific app’s support to tell me that their app had a basic function it does not have. I would love if Apple would refund me for the cost of this purchase given how awful my experience with it was and how awful their support was in using it.

reviews.title: twice charges! SCAM
reviews.text: I wanted to try the application first and see if it worked well for me. When I decided to continue using it, I get offer and I ungraded for annual subscription. However, the weekly subscription did not stop and continued to charge me for five weeks. I was paying twice for the same application. In the end, the extra charges cost more than the annual subscription itself. They said I have two Apple subscriptions - so the upgrade make a new subscription? This is NOT MY FAULT.. They told me to ask refund from apple, who rejected my request!! Very nice way to earn money

reviews.title: Widgets do not work

For a company that charges $60 a year, you would think they would make sure all the components of their app worked. Extremely disappointed in this app quality

reviews.title: Stuck with an app I don’t even like
reviews.text: There’s no trial version of this app. They pretty much force you to purchase a subscription. I have clear fitness and nutrition goals and wanted to try this app out. This app is not made for petite bodies. My caloric deficit is going to be much smaller than a taller person. I also know I need to prioritize protein to meet my goals. Per instructions by the in app support, I requested a refund through the App Store. Twice it was declined. Now I’m stuck with a membership I don’t even want.

reviews.title: Great app but a big bug
reviews.text: So I really like the app it works well but I needed to change my goal because it had me set for loosing only 20 pounds to 2029. I needed to loose it by this summer, I didn't think it would have been that hard. So I follow the steps, remove the data from my iCloud, delete the app, and reinstall it and it still had all my old goals set! I don't know how to change it, my settings app says that there is no data installed to my phone but my whole account is still set up.

reviews.title: If you’re a UK user…
reviews.text:
Oh boy, this has been the worst use of £20 this month. When I enter foods I have to find the closet American equivalent, which is really unhelpful. As such the units are different and mind boggling, even if you change the units in your profile. 

I’m not getting any additional benefits that I wouldn’t already get in MyFitnessPal, which is the same price for Premium+ or £5 cheaper for Premium. 
The thing that excites me about MyFitnessPal is when you complete the daily diary it predicts your progress in 5 weeks time. That feels really encouraging. This app, it just logs stuff and not a lot else. 

Righto, back to MyFitnessPal.

reviews.title: Would not recommend. Far too buggy
reviews.text: From Day One, I’m having issues. I attempted to addy workouts manually, but found that the number of calories per workout that I entered did not reflect my total calories in the main menu. After restarting the app, I found that the calories did not even reflect in the workout portion. I manually deleted them in order to add them again (something I should not have to do) only to find that I can no longer edit my workouts. Now, I can only add a preset workout and then delete it. The edit function is no longer available, and even if that was ok, the calories STILL do not reflect in the workout calories portion nor in the total portion. Waste of money for an app that was all about accessibility and convenience.

reviews.title: Terrible App
reviews.text:
I’ve been tracking food for years, and decided to give this app a try since it claims to scan food. My watermelon (2 pieces) rang in at 174 calories. Grapes rang in wrong, and a few cut up pieces of sweet potatoes rang it at 500+. I reached out to the app via their support chat, and was told to check  with other sources when it comes to the calories being off. Which? Is a crazy thing to say when I signed up to pay for an app to know& track calories. I cancelled the subscription same day, and am now working to get my money back from Apple. 

Save yourself the time, this app has a lot of work to be done before it’s accurate
